summary: Orchestrated ephemeral research sandboxes: auto-create Jira project/templates + Confluence playbook + Slack ephemeral channel with approval/gating
summary_long: Request to implement a single, auditable automation that provisions short-lived research sandboxes for Model Eval and Research pods. When a developer requests a sandbox via a JIRA issue, the automation should: 1) create a namespaced Jira project or project-space (scoped to the team), 2) instantiate Confluence child pages from a 'sandbox playbook' template, 3) provision a private Slack channel using enforced naming conventions and invite the requester + approvals group, 4) attach an approval step (Slack or Okta group approver) before the channel becomes active, 5) schedule automatic archival after a configurable TTL (default 30 days) with a grace-renew option, and 6) emit an audit export (S3) of channel membership and Confluence snapshot at archive time. This is intended to replace ad-hoc manual requests and ensure a reproducible, auditable lifecycle with minimal engineering touchpoints.
impact: Reduces manual overhead for platform team, speeds up Model Eval/Research experiment setup, and ensures required compliance artifacts (audit exports) are captured for internal audits. Current ad-hoc process creates inconsistent naming, missing playbooks, and undocumented Slack channels.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Creating a Jira issue in project 'Sandbox Requests' triggers the automation. 2) A Jira subproject or issue namespace is created with templated issue types (Experiment, Runbook, Cleanup). 3) Confluence page(s) created from 'Sandbox Playbook' template and linked to the Jira project. 4) Private Slack channel created with naming convention (sandbox-{team}-{shortid}), approver group notified, and channel remains muted until approver accepts. 5) Archive job triggers after TTL and stores an S3 snapshot of Confluence pages + membership CSV. 6) Logs of all steps appear in the central ops log index, and a sample audit export passes security review. 7) Automated renew (extend TTL) works from within Slack with a single command by the owner.
implementation_notes: Preferred approach: a lightweight orchestration Lambda (or internal worker) that calls the Jira REST API for project/issue templates, Confluence API for page creation, Slack SCIM / Conversations API to create channels, and Okta API to validate approver membership. Use a single service account with scoped permissions and rotate keys via KMS. Store TTL config in a small DynamoDB table keyed by sandbox id. Emit CloudWatch (or our existing observability pipeline) metrics for success/failure. See PRs referenced in related_github_prs for initial scripts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a ticket in 'Sandbox Requests' with label 'demo-sandbox' 2) Expect automation to run and create resources within ~5 minutes 3) If approver required, channel waits in dormant state until approver accepted 4) After 30 days, archival process should run and publish artifacts to S3.
notes_for_security: Security review required for: service account scope, S3 bucket lifecycle and encryption, Confluence page export sanitization (make sure secrets are redacted), Slack membership export handling. Proposed S3 path: s3://redwood-audit/sandboxes/{sandbox-id}/. Use SSE-KMS with restricted access and retention per compliance team guidance.
